description:
See or change your own system text (only your own copy; your definition and other agents do not change). One op per call:
- see: {"op": "get"}  (the whole text in effect; add "long": true for a first line FROM TAB FILE, FROM = agent (your copy), definition, or none)
- change: {"op": "set", "text": "..."}  (the whole new text, not a part of it; get it first and edit if you only want to add a line)
- undo: {"op": "reset"}  (back to your definition's text)
How it is used depends on your body: an agent-fsm brain sends it as its system message instead of the definition's (an empty text = no system message); an eca (claude, codex) appends it to the CLI's own system prompt (empty = nothing appended). It works from your next brain call (eca claude: your next turn; eca codex: your next new conversation, since codex keeps the text a conversation started with; if a person has your screen open, from when it is opened again). Each change makes your prompt cache miss once, so do not change it every turn. If you write a text that makes you unable to work, a human has to reset it. Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, SystemMissing, SystemBad, WriteFailed, DaemonMissing, DaemonFailed, InstanceMissing.

op.description: get = see your system text, set = replace it whole, reset = back to your definition's

long.description: get: first a line saying where the text comes from (agent, definition, none) and its file

text.description: set: the whole new system text ("" = none)
